title: Agent tool qualification testing
subtitle: No tool in my agent runtime ships without golden fixtures and attack fixtures, and the build fails otherwise.

stats.label: lines in the Rust test runner
platform-semantics defects the Facebook proof found, each now a test

lede: The same standard governs the social integrations: every write read back, every create with a delete, every inbound item an event. I set acceptance rules that turn "it works" into counted cases and side-channel measurements, and I make the build enforce them. Agent Swarm adds tools as YAML declarations, and I knew a tool nobody tests is the hole an agent eventually finds. So a tool without fixtures fails the build, and attack fixtures are required even for one-line tools, because exceptions to a safety rule are where the holes appear.
quote: A write whose outcome is uncertain is reconciled and cleaned up, and never resent, because on a social platform a duplicate does more harm than a gap.
evidence: Test engineering for AI agent tools: a Rust runner that sends every fixture through the real invocation harness, 50 golden fixtures for 40 declarative tools, and a build that fails on a tool without fixtures.
API qualification by parameter class: an X module qualified across 35 tools and 203 parameters with 1,010 calls and 872 asserted cases, then 505 invocations against the metered API.
Side-channel measurement in integration testing: a Facebook proof harness that blocked and counted every HTTP request outside a tool body and found 3 platform-semantics defects, each now a test.
author: Corey James
